Water evaporates into the atmosphere, and it can return to Earth's surface as rain or snow. This continuous motion of water is known as the

contents.text: This diagram is a model of the water cycle. It shows some of the processes that move water through the atmosphere, across Earth's surface, and under the ground.

pieces.text: Most liquid water on Earth is found in bodies of water such as oceans, lakes, and rivers. As these bodies of water are warmed by the Sun, some of the water at the surface changes from a liquid to a gas called water vapor. The process of water changing from a liquid to a gas at the surface of an ocean, lake, or river is called

Though water vapor is not visible, it makes up part of the air that surrounds us. When water vapor rises in the atmosphere, it can cool down enough to form water droplets around particles in the air, changing back into liquid water. The liquid water is visible in the form of clouds. The process of water changing from a gas to a liquid is called

Clouds are made of many tiny water droplets and ice crystals. If these water droplets and ice crystals become large enough, they can fall toward Earth's surface as rain, snow, sleet, or hail. The process of water falling from clouds toward Earth's surface is called

Rain that reaches Earth's surface can begin to move downhill, and it may become part of a stream or river. Snow and ice that reach Earth's surface can melt and flow along the surface as liquid water. The process of water flowing along the surface of Earth is called
